body_text: View all news AXT Announces Jia-Bin Duh Appointed to AXT, Inc. Board of Directors 07/22/2026 Download (opens in new window) FREMONT, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- AXT, Inc. (NasdaqGS: AXTI), a leading manufacturer of compound semiconductor wafer substrates, today announced that Jia-Bin Duh has been appointed to the AXT Board of Directors, effective July 16, 2026. The AXT Board expanded to six directors from the previous number of five. Duh brings more than 30 years of senior executive leadership and investor experience across the technology and consumer sectors, with deep expertise in international business operations, strategic growth, and Greater China markets. Throughout his career, he has held senior leadership positions at several leading technology companies, including Hewlett-Packard, Microsoft, and Cisco Systems, where he led business expansion and operations throughout China. His executive experience operating in the region, together with his understanding of its commercial and regulatory environment, will provide valuable perspective as AXT continues to grow its global business and support the long-term success of Tongmei, the Company's subsidiary in China. Duh currently serves as Director of Primax Electronics Ltd. (TPE: 4915), a position he has held since 2021, where he also served as Chairman and Chief Executive Officer from 2023-2024. Duh has also served as Chairman of Mobinnova Corp. from 2006-2009. Throughout his career, Duh held top leadership positions at major multinational corporations including serving as President of Cisco Systems China from 1998 to 2005 and Corporate Vice President of Cisco Systems Inc., and as President of Microsoft China from 1993 to 1998. Duh has served as an independent director of Wangfujing International Group Ltd. (SHA 600859) from 2016-2019, IDT International Limited (HK: 0167) from 2015-2018 and Huizhou Tymphany Acoustics Technology Ltd. Duh received a Bachelor of Science degree in Control Engineering from National Chiao Tung University, a Master of Business Administration from the Kellogg School of Management at Northwestern University and a Master of Business Administration from the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology. “We are pleased to welcome Jia-Bin to the AXT Board of Directors,” said Morris Young, chief executive officer. “Jia-Bin brings exceptional leadership experience gained from building and leading businesses across Greater China for some of the world's premier technology companies. His deep understanding of the Chinese business environment, strong relationships across both the public and private sectors, and extensive public company board experience will be invaluable as we continue to execute our long-term growth strategy and expand our global leadership in compound semiconductor substrates.” About AXT, Inc. AXT is a material science company that develops and manufactures high-performance compound and single element semiconductor substrate wafers comprising indium phosphide (InP), gallium arsenide (GaAs) and germanium (Ge). The company’s substrate wafers are used when a typical silicon substrate wafer cannot meet the performance requirements of a semiconductor or optoelectronic device. End markets include AI/data center connectivity, 5G infrastructure, passive optical networks, LED lighting, lasers, sensors, power amplifiers for wireless devices and satellite solar cells. AXT’s worldwide headquarters are in Fremont, California where the company maintains sales, administration and customer service functions. AXT has its Asia headquarters in Beijing, China and manufacturing facilities in three separate locations in China. In addition, as part of its supply chain strategy, the company has partial ownership in over ten companies in China producing raw materials for its manufacturing process. For more information, see AXT’s website at https://investors.axt.com . title: Formulary Flip: Making Your Drug List Work for You
body_text: When was the last time you evaluated your formulary? During your last annual review? If so, you might be in for a surprise. A lot can change in a year, and you might be facing sky high prescription costs you never signed up for. The reason? Your PBM. If you've been following our blog, you know we often point a finger at PBMs (link to previous posts). Employers typically hire PBMs to put together a list of prescriptions, otherwise known as a formulary, that provide the best value. However, PBMs don't always have the employer's best intentions in mind. Instead, they sometimes use this opportunity to slip in high-cost drugs, reaping high rebates at the expense of the employer. If plan sponsors don’t frequently review their formulary, these sneaky moves can go unnoticed, leading to increased drug spending without anyone being the wiser. In fact, a recent report from the Delaware state auditor highlighted this issue, revealing that Express Scripts overcharged the state employee prescription drug plan by $24.5 million. They did this by including more expensive drugs in the formulary without clearly informing the state about the implications. The takeaway? Knowing and actively managing your formulary can save you thousands if not millions. That’s why in this post, we're diving deep into formulary and plan design as a cost-saving strategy. We'll explore cost-efficient plan design options and share best practices you can implement right away—even if you’re not ready to change up your formulary just yet. So, let’s get started! Changing Things Up When it comes to optimizing your formulary, few strategies are as effective as implementing a tiered pharmacy benefit plan. It's no wonder that, as of 2023, 92% of health plans incorporate some kind of tiered structure. But why are these plans so popular? Simply put, they offer a clever way to save money for both patients and the plan itself by incentivizing the use of less expensive generics. Here's how it works: In a tiered plan, the drugs in the formulary are separated into different tiers based on their cost. The least expensive drugs, like generics, are placed in the lowest tier, while more expensive, brand-name drugs occupy the higher tiers. This setup isn't just for show—it's designed to make the economic value of each drug crystal clear to patients. ‍ ‍ Let's break it down with a simple example. Imagine a three-tier system where the copayments are structured as follows: $5 for first-tier (cheapest) drugs, $15 for second-tier drugs, and $45 for third-tier (most expensive) drugs. If a patient is prescribed a drug in the third tier but finds a clinically similar option in the first tier, they can choose the cheaper one and save money. If they decide to stick with the more expensive option due to personal preference or other factors, they bear the additional cost themselves, rather than passing it on to the plan. This tiered approach encourages patients to be more economically conscious about their healthcare spending. By making them more aware of the cost implications of their choices, the plan not only saves money but also becomes more economically efficient. It’s a win-win situation where everyone benefits—patients get the medication they need at a lower cost, and the plan avoids unnecessary expenses. So, next time you're considering how to optimize your formulary, think about giving tiered copayments a try. It's like giving your formulary a smart financial makeover! This tiered approach nudges patients to be more mindful of their healthcare spending. It highlights the cost implications of their choices, helping everyone save money. In theory it’s a win-win: patients pay less for the meds they need, and the plan avoids extra costs! ‍ How Savings are Made Now that you're familiar with how tiered healthcare plans operate, let's explore how they contribute to cost savings. These plans leverage two main strategies: guiding patients towards cost-effective drug choices and reducing overall prescription volume. Together, these strategies can significantly reduce healthcare expenses and make managing a plan's budget more manageable. 1. Encouraging Economically Savvy Choices We've touched on this already: tiered plans guide patients toward more affordable drug options by offering lower copayments for cheaper medications. When patients opt for these less expensive alternatives, the plan's share of the costs decreases, leading to significant savings. For instance, a report by Express Scripts suggests that shifting to a three-tiered plan can cut overall drug costs by 7-8% simply due to changes in consumer purchasing behavior. 2. Reducing Prescription Volume Tiered plans can also lower the total number of prescriptions filled, particularly for higher-cost drugs. The increased copayments for these medications might lead some patients to skip them altogether, saving the plan additional costs. A study found that switching from a non-tiered to a three-tiered plan resulted in a 14.6% drop in the total number of prescriptions filled. While this data comes from elderly plan members, it's likely that a similar trend would be seen in a working-age population. However, there's a flip side. Critics argue that reduced prescription use isn't always a good thing, especially if it means patients skip necessary medications for chronic conditions. If a plan isn't monitoring adherence, savings from fewer prescriptions could be offset by increased ER visits and hospitalizations due to untreated conditions. That's why it's crucial to use effective analytics to monitor adherence so that less prescriptions are filled only for unnecessary drugs. If there are adherence issues for serious conditions you should take action, like offering patient education or enhanced support for those needing pricier meds. By focusing on eliminating spending on unnecessary high-cost, low-value drugs, while still ensuring patients get their essential medications, savings could soar up to 24%! And if you're wondering how to keep track of all this, good news! At TrueClaim, we offer an AI-powered hub to analyze your healthcare data, ensuring no discrepancies slip through the cracks. This way, you can fully harness the cost-saving potential of a tiered system. Best Practices Of course switching to a multi-tiered plan might not always be possible, but there are still effective strategies you can use to manage your formulary and reduce healthcare costs. Here are some practical steps you can take to optimize your current setup without making a complete overhaul. 1. Evaluate Your Current Formulary and PBM Contract Start by thoroughly reviewing your current formulary and the terms of your PBM contract. As we mentioned earlier, PBMs often update formularies without always clearly communicating those changes. It's crucial to audit your drug list regularly to spot any high-cost, low-value medications that may have been slipped in. 2. Identify Potentially Wasteful Drugs Keep an eye out for combination drugs, which often come with a hefty price tag compared to purchasing the active ingredients separately. These can be a sneaky way of inflating costs without providing additional value. If you find such drugs in your formulary, consult your PBM about generic alternatives. Generics typically offer the same efficacy as brand-name drugs but at a fraction of the cost. 3. Consult Your PBM for Cost Analysis Ask your PBM to provide a cost analysis comparing your current formulary with a proposed list that includes more cost-effective alternatives. This comparison can help you visualize potential savings and ensure you're getting the best value. 4. Negotiate with Your PBM If your PBM is hesitant to adjust the formulary, don't hesitate to negotiate. You can request a higher percentage of rebate dollars or offer to pay an additional fee for a customized plan. Often, the savings from an optimized formulary can outweigh these costs, making it a worthwhile investment. The bottom line is: Don't be afraid to ask tough questions and demand better options. A simple "no" shouldn't be the end of the conversation. If you're not getting the answers or the savings you're looking for, it might be time to consider switching PBMs or even rethinking your plan entirely. ‍ Wrapping Things Up So there you have it! Managing your formulary effectively can make a world of difference in controlling healthcare costs. Whether it's embracing a multi-tiered plan or simply staying vigilant with your current setup, the key is to be proactive. Regularly evaluate your formulary, keep an eye out for costly, low-value drugs, and don't be afraid to negotiate with your PBM. Remember, every decision you make can contribute to significant savings for your plan and your members. At the end of the day, it's all about ensuring that your healthcare plan is as efficient and cost-effective as possible. And if you're feeling overwhelmed, tools like TrueClaim's AI-powered hub can help you stay on top of everything. So go ahead, take charge of your formulary, and watch those savings add up! ‍

title: Responding to an IRS Exempt Status Examination: A Guide for Not-for-Profit Organizations
summary: Learn how not-for-profit organizations can respond to an IRS exempt status examination, manage risks, and protect tax-exempt status.
body_text: An IRS examination of a not-for-profit’s exempt status, or the risk of revocation, can feel high stakes and disruptive. While the process is serious, the most effective response is not reactive. A calm, organized, and disciplined approach can help protect your mission and position your organization for a more favorable outcome. The practical steps below reflect what often proves effective when the IRS scrutinizes exempt status. Respond Quickly and Get Organized Treat IRS correspondence as time sensitive from the moment it arrives. Open the letter immediately, calendar all deadlines, and assign clear ownership. Missing a response date can limit your options and escalate issues unnecessarily. Designate a single point of contact to manage communications with the IRS. Acknowledge receipt of the notice promptly, and if additional time is needed, request a reasonable extension in writing. Maintain a detailed log of all correspondence and documents shared throughout the examination. Before engaging with the IRS, prepare deliberately. Review the standard audit questionnaire with your CPA and/or attorney before any conversations take place. Gather and reconcile key materials, including governing documents, Forms 990 , financial statements, board minutes, policies, program descriptions, and fundraising records. Your goal is consistency: ensuring your documentation and explanations clearly align with your original exempt purpose and demonstrate how current activities further that purpose. Prepare for IRS Meetings and Interviews Use early interactions with the IRS to listen carefully and clarify scope. Initial meetings often provide insight into the agent’s focus areas, perceived risks, and framing of the examination. Pay close attention to the questions asked and comments made because they can signal where the IRS is concentrating its review. Take contemporaneous notes during all meetings. Ask the agent to explain what information they need and why, and confirm your understanding of issues, expectations, and next steps in writing after each interaction. During interviews, maintain strict factual discipline. A few ground rules can help keep responses accurate and controlled: Answer only the question asked; avoid volunteering additional information. Stick to verifiable facts. Do not speculate or offer opinions. If you do not know an answer, say so and offer to follow up. Assume every response becomes part of the IRS administrative record and may be reviewed by managers, Appeals, or Chief Counsel. Handle Information Document Requests Strategically Information Document Requests (IDRs) deserve careful attention. How, and how quickly, you respond can influence the pace, clarity, and direction of the examination. Consider preparing a concise written narrative that outlines your organization’s structure, mission, programs, funding sources, and the facts supporting your exempt status. This context can help the IRS better understand the documents you provide and reduce misinterpretation. When responding to IDRs: Never ignore or leave a request incomplete. If the IRS focuses on a known risk area, assess the facts early, remediate where possible, and be prepared to explain the issue clearly. Produce only what is responsive to the request. Keep copies of everything you submit and consider indexing materials to improve clarity and organization. Work With Experienced Not-for-Profit Tax Advisors Do not navigate an exempt status examination alone. Engage a CPA and/or attorney with experience in not-for-profit tax controversy. The right advisors can help frame issues effectively, preserve privilege where applicable, coordinate responses, and guide you through Appeals if necessary. Handled thoughtfully, an IRS examination does not have to derail your operations or distract from your mission. Process discipline, factual clarity, and experienced guidance remain your strongest tools for managing and resolving an exempt status examination. Next Steps If your organization is facing an IRS exempt status examination, connect with our not-for-profit tax specialists for guidance on responding strategically and protecting your exempt status. Frequently Asked Questions An IRS exempt status examination is a review of whether a not-for-profit organization continues to meet the requirements for tax-exempt status under the Internal Revenue Code. The IRS evaluates governing documents, Forms 990, financial records, programs, and operations to determine whether activities align with the organization’s stated exempt purpose. These examinations may arise from routine compliance reviews, targeted enforcement initiatives, or identified risk indicators. A not-for-profit should respond to an IRS audit or examination notice promptly and in an organized manner. Best practices include calendaring deadlines, designating a single point of contact, and consulting with experienced not-for-profit tax advisors before engaging with the IRS. Responses should be factual, complete, and limited to what is requested. Thoughtful handling of Information Document Requests (IDRs) and careful preparation for interviews can help manage risk and keep the examination focused. IRS exempt organization examinations involve technical rules and potentially significant consequences, including penalties or revocation of tax-exempt status. CPAs and attorneys with not-for-profit tax controversy experience can help frame issues appropriately, coordinate responses, preserve privilege where applicable, and guide organizations through the Appeals process if needed. title: Citibank virtual card: How to get one and use it safely
summary: Need a Citibank virtual card for online shopping? Learn how to generate a virtual account number, where to use it, and the best alternatives. Compare today.
body_text: Every time you shop online, your payment details pass through multiple systems before reaching the merchant. While most transactions are completed safely, data breaches, phishing attacks and card theft remain common concerns for online shoppers. That's why many banks have introduced virtual payment tools that help customers protect their real card numbers without changing the way they shop. Citibank's solution is Citi Virtual Account Numbers (VAN), a feature that generates a temporary card number linked to your eligible Citi credit card. Instead of sharing your actual card details with every merchant, you can use the virtual number for online purchases, reducing the risk if a retailer's payment system is compromised. This guide explains how Citi Virtual Account Numbers work, who can use them, how to generate one, the security benefits they offer and the situations where a virtual card is a smarter choice than using your physical card online. Also read: How to shop in the US or Europe with your Grey card What is a Citibank virtual card? Shopping online is convenient, but every purchase also means trusting another merchant with your card details. To reduce that risk, Citibank introduced Citi Virtual Account Numbers (VAN), a security feature that lets eligible cardholders generate a temporary card number linked to their existing Citi credit card. The virtual number can be used instead of your actual card number when making online purchases, helping keep your real payment details private if a merchant experiences a data breach or security incident. Citi Virtual Account Numbers are available to eligible Citi credit cardholders, although availability depends on your card type and location. Citibank offers this feature to give customers greater protection against online fraud while maintaining the convenience of card payments. Because each virtual number is tied to your Citi account rather than replacing it, purchases, rewards and billing continue to work as they normally would, but with an added layer of security for online transactions. How to find your Citibank virtual card number Eligible Citi cardholders can create a Virtual Account Number through their online account, customise its settings and start using it for secure online purchases within minutes. Sign in: Log in to your Citi Online account using your username and password, then access the credit card eligible for Citi Virtual Account Numbers. Open card: Select your eligible Citi credit card and navigate to the Virtual Account Numbers feature, where you can create and manage temporary card numbers. Create number: Generate a new Virtual Account Number and customise settings such as the expiration date and spending limit to suit your planned purchase. View details: Once generated, copy the virtual card number, expiration date and security code displayed on the screen for your online transaction. Use online: Enter the Virtual Account Number at checkout instead of your physical card details to complete eligible online purchases with an added layer of security. Also read: How to pay online and in stores worldwide with your phone Best ways to use your Citibank virtual card for safer online payments Citibank Virtual Account Numbers are most effective for online purchases where extra security matters, helping protect your real card details without changing how you pay. Subscription services: Use a Virtual Account Number when paying for streaming platforms, software licences or cloud storage. Setting an expiration date or spending limit can help you manage recurring payments and reduce the impact of unauthorised charges if your payment details are compromised. One-time purchases: When shopping from a retailer you don't expect to use again, generate a new Virtual Account Number instead of sharing your permanent card details. This keeps your actual Citi card number hidden while completing the purchase normally. Unfamiliar websites: Buying from a merchant you've never used before carries some risk. A Citibank Virtual Account Number adds another layer of protection because the temporary number can be limited or replaced without affecting your physical credit card. Checkout process: Enter the Virtual Account Number, expiration date and security code exactly as you would a regular Citi credit card. If the merchant accepts Mastercard or Visa, depending on your Citi card, the payment is processed through your linked account. What are the limitations of a Citibank virtual card? Citi Virtual Account Numbers improve online payment security, but they are not available to every Citi customer. Not all Citi credit cards support the feature, and availability may vary by card type and country. Before looking for the option in your online account, confirm that your card is eligible for Citi Virtual Account Numbers. There are also practical limitations to keep in mind. Virtual Account Numbers are designed primarily for online purchases and generally cannot be used for in-store transactions. Some merchants that require the original card at the point of collection, such as certain hotels or car rental companies, may reject them. In addition, some recurring subscriptions and automatic billing arrangements may not work if the virtual number expires or reaches its spending limit. Finally, not every online merchant accepts virtual card numbers, so your physical Citi card may still be needed in some situations. Also read: Grey card vs other virtual cards: What you should know Best alternatives to Citibank virtual cards If your Citi card isn't eligible or you need more flexibility, several banks and fintech companies offer virtual cards designed for different spending needs and international payments. Grey virtual card: Best for freelancers, remote workers and global earners. Fund your virtual Visa card with USD, GBP or EUR balances and use it for secure online shopping and international payments. Capital One: Eligible Capital One credit cardholders can generate virtual card numbers for online purchases, making it a strong option for customers who already bank within the Capital One ecosystem. Chase: Selected Chase credit cards include virtual card features that help protect your actual card number during online shopping while maintaining access to your existing rewards and account benefits. Wise: Wise offers virtual cards in supported regions, making them ideal for travellers and international shoppers who regularly spend across multiple currencies using their Wise account balance. Revolut: Revolut provides standard and disposable virtual cards, giving users extra protection when shopping online or paying unfamiliar merchants while managing spending directly from the app. Bank virtual cards: Many traditional banks now offer virtual card numbers for eligible credit cardholders. If you already have a credit card, check with your bank before opening a new account elsewhere. Frequently asked questions Do all Citibank cards support virtual card numbers? No. Citi Virtual Account Numbers are only available on eligible Citi credit cards, and availability depends on your card product and country. If you can't find the feature in your online account, your card may not qualify. Check Citi's documentation or contact customer support to confirm eligibility. Can I use a Citibank virtual card for subscriptions? Sometimes, but it depends on how you've configured the virtual number. If the card expires or has a spending limit that is reached, recurring payments may fail. For long-term subscriptions, it's important to choose settings that remain valid for the entire billing period. How long does a Citibank virtual card number stay active? A Citi Virtual Account Number remains active until the expiration date you choose or until it is cancelled, depending on the available settings. If the number expires before a merchant processes another payment, future transactions using that virtual number will be declined. Can I generate multiple Citibank virtual cards? Yes. Eligible Citi cardholders can generate multiple Virtual Account Numbers for different online purchases. Using separate numbers for different merchants helps reduce risk and makes it easier to replace a compromised virtual number without affecting payments made to other retailers. What is the best alternative for international online shopping? If you frequently buy from international websites or pay in foreign currencies, a virtual card linked to a multi-currency account is often the better choice. Platforms like Grey let you hold USD, GBP and EUR, making international online payments more convenient and cost-effective. How do I get a Grey virtual card? Open a Grey account, complete the required identity verification and fund your supported foreign currency wallet. Once you're eligible, you can instantly create a Grey virtual Visa card in the app and start paying securely at online merchants that accept Mastercard worldwide. Citi Virtual Account Numbers add an extra layer of security to online shopping, but they aren't available to every cardholder. For a virtual Mastercard built for global spending, open a Grey account or download the app to get instant access and pay online using your USD, GBP or EUR balance.

body_text: Switching to a cybersecurity career is more achievable than ever, especially with the right ethical hacking certification. If you are looking to break into roles like penetration tester, red teamer, or security analyst, choosing the right certification can help you stand out to employers, validate your skills, and unlock higher salaries. This guide is specifically designed for adults pivoting into IT or cybersecurity, entry-level professionals ready to move up, and anyone who wants practical, job-ready skills validated by industry-recognized credentials. Which Ethical Hacking Certification Is Best for Career Changers? The top ethical hacking certifications for career changers are OSCP, CEH, and eJPT. OSCP is highly valued for advanced, hands-on penetration testing; CEH is widely recognized for foundational and compliance roles; and eJPT is an ideal entry point for beginners. The best choice depends on your current experience and career goals. Why Ethical Hacking Certifications Matter in 2026 With cyber threats becoming more advanced, the demand for skilled ethical hackers has soared. Employers rely on certifications as a key hiring filter, especially for candidates without a traditional tech degree. According to recent studies, 91% of cybersecurity employers prefer or require certifications. Ethical hacking certifications demonstrate both practical and theoretical knowledge, boosting your chances of landing interviews, promotions, and higher salaries. For career changers, veterans, and tech enthusiasts, certifications are a powerful way to prove your readiness for real-world cybersecurity roles. They also offer a clear path to move from entry-level jobs to specialized positions like penetration tester or security consultant. OSCP: The Gold Standard for Hands-On Penetration Testing What Is the OSCP? The Offensive Security Certified Professional (OSCP) is renowned for its rigorous, practical exam and is often called the "gold standard" for penetration testing. It is sought after by employers for red team, offensive security, and advanced pentesting roles. Key Features and Latest Updates Dual credential: Lifetime OSCP and renewable OSCP+ (valid for 3 years). Heavily focused on real-world attack scenarios, especially Windows Active Directory. Exam is 100% hands-on: 23 hours 45 minutes to compromise multiple targets, followed by a 24-hour report submission window. Requires deep skills in Linux, Windows, scripting, and privilege escalation. No more bonus points for course exercises; exam performance alone determines the result. OSCP is best suited for those with some IT or security background, ideally after earning a foundational credential like eJPT or CompTIA Security+. Career Impact and ROI OSCP holders are highly employable, with 92% reporting promotions within a year of certification. Salaries typically range from $120,000 to $158,000 or more in the US. This credential opens doors to senior technical roles and is recognized worldwide. Certified Ethical Hacker (CEH): Broad Recognition and Compliance Who Should Consider CEH? The Certified Ethical Hacker (CEH), from EC-Council, is designed for IT professionals, network admins, and new security analysts. It is especially valuable for those targeting compliance-focused or government jobs, as well as those who want a wide overview of hacking techniques. What Is Covered in CEH? 20 modules across all major ethical hacking topics: reconnaissance, scanning, system and network hacking, malware, social engineering, IoT/OT security, and more. Latest versions (v13/v14) incorporate AI-powered labs, simulated hacking exercises, and current threat intelligence (including MITRE ATT&CK, APTs, ransomware). Exam includes a 4-hour, 125-question theory component, and an optional 6-hour practical lab (for CEH Master). Prerequisites are moderate: two years' info security experience or completion of official training. CEH is considered moderately difficult, with the main challenge being the breadth of content. Industry Value CEH is widely recognized by government and enterprise employers. It is often listed as a requirement in cybersecurity job postings, especially for security analyst, penetration tester, and compliance-focused roles. Average US salaries are $87,877 to $126,547, and top performers can earn more. CEH is also recommended for those pursuing DoD 8570/8140 compliance careers. eJPT: The Best Entry-Level Practical Ethical Hacking Certification What Is the eJPT? The eLearnSecurity Junior Penetration Tester (eJPT) is a 100% hands-on certification built for beginners and career changers. It requires no formal prerequisites, making it an excellent first step for those new to cybersecurity or penetration testing. What Does the eJPT Cover? Network and web application scanning, vulnerability assessment, and exploitation basics. Privilege escalation, post-exploitation, and basic persistence techniques. Real-world skills: using tools like Nmap, Metasploit, Hydra, and Kali Linux. 48-hour practical exam, completed in-browser, with challenges that require active exploitation and flag retrieval. The eJPT is recognized as a "first foot in the door" for cybersecurity roles. Passing validates your readiness for junior penetration tester and entry-level security analyst positions. US salaries typically range from $70,000 to $90,500 for these roles. Choosing the Right Ethical Hacking Certification for Your Career Path Selecting the right ethical hacking certification depends on your background and target role: Absolute beginners should start with eJPT or CompTIA Security+ to build foundational skills. IT professionals or help desk staff ready to move into cybersecurity can pursue CEH for broad, employer-recognized validation. Those aiming for advanced penetration testing roles should prepare for OSCP after gaining foundational experience. Certification stacking is a smart strategy. For example, many professionals earn eJPT or Security+ first, then CEH, and finally pursue OSCP to maximize both marketability and earnings. For more on entry-level certifications and career roadmaps, see our Network Engineer Program + Cybersecurity Accelerator which combines hands-on training, live instruction, and expert career coaching to guide you from zero to hired in IT or cybersecurity. How to Prepare for Ethical Hacking Certification Success 1. Assess Your Experience Level Analyze your current technical foundation. Beginners should focus on networking and basic security before jumping into advanced certifications. 2. Choose the Right Training Approach Combine self-study, instructor-led courses, and hands-on labs for the best results. Practical lab work is essential, especially for OSCP and eJPT. 3. Practice with Real-World Scenarios Simulate exam environments, use practice tests, and document your exercises. Many certifications require a report or proof of your hands-on work. 4. Plan for Renewal and Continuing Education Keep your certifications active by earning Continuing Professional Education (CPE) credits or taking renewal exams. This shows employers your commitment to staying current in the fast-evolving cybersecurity landscape. Ready to Launch Your Ethical Hacking Career? Whether you are a career changer, veteran, or aspiring security professional, the right ethical hacking certification can accelerate your journey into high-demand cybersecurity roles. Certifications like OSCP, CEH, and eJPT provide a structured path to mastering real-world skills, proving your value to employers, and achieving life-changing career growth. It is ideal for those new to cybersecurity or penetration testing. How do OSCP, CEH, and eJPT differ in difficulty and recognition? OSCP is the most challenging and respected for advanced pentesting, CEH offers broad recognition and is moderately difficult, while eJPT is entry-level and accessible to motivated learners. Do I need a degree for ethical hacking certifications? No, most ethical hacking certifications do not require a college degree. They focus on skills and practical knowledge, making them accessible to career changers and those without traditional backgrounds. How long does it take to prepare for an ethical hacking certification? Preparation time varies: eJPT can be completed in a few months, CEH often takes three to six months, and OSCP may require six months or more of dedicated hands-on practice. Quarterly Highlights Core Contract Awards SLB continues to win new contract awards that align with SLB’s strengths in the Core. Notable highlights include the following: In the Gulf of America, SLB OneSubsea joint venture was awarded a contract by bp to provide a subsea boosting system for the Thunder Horse deepwater development project. This engineering, procurement and construction contract for Thunder Horse follows recent subsea boosting contract awards for bp’s Kaskida and Tiber developments. All three projects leverage the same supplier-led, standardized subsea boosting system solution, which helps improve execution efficiency and shorten delivery times. Also, in the Gulf of America, SLB OneSubsea was awarded a contract by Beacon Offshore Energy Exploration and Production LLC to deliver a high‑pressure, high‑temperature (HPHT) multiphase boosting system for the Shenandoah field. The award reflects continued investment in deepwater developments, where advanced subsea production systems are being applied to improve recovery. OneSubsea’s HPHT multiphase boosting system is engineered to operate reliably above 15,000 psi, addressing operating conditions that exceed the limits of conventional subsea solutions. Offshore Indonesia, SLB OneSubsea was awarded a contract by Eni North Ganal Limited (a subsidiary of Searah Limited, a joint venture company between Eni and PETRONAS) to deliver a steel tube umbilical system for the Kutei North Hub field development project in East Kalimantan. Supporting one of the region’s most significant deepwater developments, OneSubsea will engineer, procure and manufacture 94.6 kilometers of umbilical for water depths of up to 2,200 meters. Also in Kuwait, KOC awarded SLB a five-year contract to deliver bits for both land and offshore drilling operations as well as a significant contract award for cementing and related services in conventional and unconventional scopes. SLB will deploy advanced bits and reverse circulation technologies tailored for KOC’s subsurface environment, addressing the complexity of local geological conditions. These high-performance drilling solutions are engineered to enhance efficiency and reduce well construction costs. The cementing award underscores SLB’s commitment to innovative technologies, operational excellence and sustainable value — all while supporting KOC in driving safety, performance and long-term value creation in Kuwait. In India, Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) awarded SLB a significant deepwater drilling contract to support the drilling of 24 wells over four years for its offshore energy development. Under the agreement, SLB will deliver integrated drilling services and technologies to support efficient execution in complex deepwater environments. The project supports ONGC’s strategy to accelerate domestic hydrocarbon production through efficient and cost-effective offshore development while reinforcing SLB’s position as a trusted partner for complex deepwater projects in India. PTT Exploration and Production (PTTEP) awarded SLB a two-year managed pressure drilling (MPD) contract for offshore exploration. Technology Highlights Notable technology introductions and deployments in the quarter include the following: During the inaugural SLB Production and Recovery Summit, SLB launched its Intelligent Production Studio, an environment for digital operations. The live operating environment integrates AI, edge intelligence, connected equipment, digital twins and autonomous workflows, to show an intelligent production system in action. Built around a fully autonomous well pad managing real three-phase flow of oil, water and gas across multiple well streams, the studio enables customers to evaluate interconnected, intelligent production systems before field deployment. The facility models surveillance, anomaly detection, robotic inspection, autonomous chemical injection and closed-loop optimization to aid in field design decisions. SLB launched AlphaSight™, the company’s latest innovation in reservoir mapping and drilling intelligence. The AlphaSight service leverages industry-first technologies, setting a new benchmark for visibility and control in complex drilling environments to maximize production potential. Designed to deliver clearer subsurface insight at significantly further depths, the AlphaSight service helps operators see and understand reservoir structures in real time — supporting confident drilling decisions without slowing performance. Retina™ at-bit imaging system achieved strong market adoption in its first year of commercialization, with deployments in more than 50 wells across 16 locations worldwide and over 122,000 feet of data acquired. By providing high-resolution formation measurements at first contact with the rock, the Retina system delivers earlier subsurface visibility, helping operators reduce uncertainty and make more informed drilling, completion and reservoir development decisions. Successful deployments in the Gulf of America, U.S. land, East Asia and the Middle East demonstrated the system’s value across a wide range of geological and operational environments, reinforcing its growing role in improving well placement and reservoir understanding. In North Africa, SLB applied an integrated approach, focusing on production enhancement, to help an operator rejuvenate a 50-year-old mature onshore field challenged by declining production, rising water cut, idle wells and legacy facilities. The multidisciplinary solution combined advanced reservoir diagnostics, targeted well interventions, facility debottlenecking and digital operations under a unified delivery model. The project unlocked 13.8 million barrels of incremental oil, delivered production results three times higher than initial forecasts, brought 90 wells online and reduced produced water volumes by 55%, demonstrating the impact of SLB’s integrated technology and execution model in improving recovery and operational efficiency across mature assets. In the United Arab Emirates, SLB collaborated with a national oil company to reactivate shut-in wells in a mature onshore field using Production Express™ rapid production response solutions. The mobile surface multiphase boosting deployment increased wellhead pressure by 300 psi, restoring stable production of more than 3 million standard cubic feet per day of gas and more than 7,000 barrels per day of liquids. The solution enabled zero-flaring operations, reduced emissions for the operator and established a qualified pathway for future multiphase boosting and zero-flaring projects across onshore and offshore wells. Following commercialization in the first quarter of 2026, SLB's automated cementing technology has rapidly evolved from a pioneering digital innovation into a scalable commercial solution. Building on the industry's first fully automated cementing job in Norway, the technology has now surpassed 100 remote and automated cementing jobs, validating years of investment in automation, digital workflows and remote operations. Additionally, a key milestone was recently achieved with its first deployment in Egypt, where the cementing team successfully executed an automated dual-slurry operation on Shell's Velox-1 well, demonstrating the technology's scalability and supporting SLB's competitive differentiation in digital well construction. In the Gulf of America, SLB helped restore production from a deepwater well that had been shut in for nearly four years because of sand production challenges. Using RemedySlot™ through tubing sand screens as a targeted remedial solution, SLB avoided a full recompletion and completed the intervention in 101 hours. The well returned to stable production of more than 900 barrels per day, protecting critical subsea equipment and recovering value for the customer. Across Kuwait, SLB and KOC advanced integrated water-control and injector-conformance workflows, combining powered, fiber-optic ACTive™ real-time downhole coiled tubing services, high-resolution diagnostics and engineered chemical water shutoff systems to restore reservoir performance without conventional rig workover. Across three producer and injector interventions, the workflows reduced water cut, improved injection conformance and delivered measurable oil production gains. Results included uplift to about 975 and 1,200 barrels of oil per day in two producers. The injector intervention also delivered approximately 2,100 barrels of oil per day of incremental oil from five surrounding producers, demonstrating a repeatable diagnose-to-remediate model for improved recovery. Better-connected decisions enabled fewer, more effective interventions to reduce cost while sustaining production. Within Digital, revenue is generated from four key solutions — Platforms & Applications, Digital Operations, Digital Exploration and Professional Services. Platforms & Applications includes SLB’s cloud technologies such as the Delfi™ and Lumi™ platforms, along with a suite of specialized, domain-focused applications such as Petrel™ and Techlog™ offered as SaaS subscription or perpetual licenses. These platforms and applications automate complex models to simulate the impact of reservoir development plans and aid in the planning of key operations such as drilling, completion and production designs. Additionally, they unlock data and utilize AI and machine learning to reduce cycle time and improve efficiency of workflows to allow customers to make better, faster decisions to improve their project economics and reservoir performance. Revenue is recurring (with exception of one-off license sales) underpinned by a substantial base of ARR from a globally installed base, complemented by customer adoption of new cloud-based capabilities and IoT-enabled solutions. This category has best-in-class retention rates and limited churn. Digital Operations combines the unique strengths of SLB’s oilfield services with advanced digital technologies to deliver more reliable, efficient and autonomous field operations. By integrating connected solutions with Performance Live™ digital service delivery centers, customers gain real-time monitoring, remote decision making and automated execution across their workflows from autonomous drilling to automated well intervention, all while reducing costs and improving project economics. Revenue is generated from the same customer base as the Core divisions and is, therefore, repeatable. Additionally, a portion of the revenue is recurring in nature. To incentivize the Core divisions — Well Construction, Reservoir Performance and Production Systems — and Digital to develop and promote this category, the resulting revenue is recognized in both the respective Core division as well as in the Digital Division. This effect is eliminated in consolidation. Digital Exploration represents SLB’s exploration data business. The exploration data library is a differentiated asset library of seismic surveys and other subsurface data that customers rely on for better exploration and development decisions. These licensed datasets also support carbon storage design and monitoring. The library covers key exploration and producing basins worldwide and datasets are refreshed and reprocessed to benefit from the latest imaging algorithms and AI technologies, enabled by high performance cloud computing. Revenue is generated from one-time, non-transferable license sales and is therefore non-recurring in nature. Professional Services includes consulting and other services required to support customers’ digital transformations. These services include transition support from on-prem to cloud-based digital solutions, data clean-up and migration, workflow automation — including deployment of workflow solutions built within SLB’s global network of Innovation Factori workspaces — and training to further enable customers’ digital transformations. Revenue in this category is largely project-based, and repetitive engagements with the same customers are common. These services generate pull-through opportunities across other digital revenue streams. 11) How much revenue was generated from each of the categories comprising the Digital Division in the first six months of 2026 and the first six months of 2025?
